messages:
maria: Quick Q — thinking about adding a lightweight 'contextual_hint' to the pin resolver so clients can nudge affinity (non-binding). Example inline: `contextual_hint: "ui=autocomplete;workload=low_latency"`. Pros/cons?

antoine: I like the UX angle. Main concerns: cache fragmentation (hints create high cardinality keys), privacy (no user identifiers), and operational complexity for eviction.

kevin: Agree on those. Can we constrain allowed hint keys to a small controlled set (enum-like) and cap size (e.g., <256 bytes)? Also need deterministic hashing function so different runtimes compute same signature.

sam: +1. Important: hints must be advisory only. They should influence scoring for routing, not create authoritative pins that affect ownership/quota. Otherwise Dedicated contracts get weird.

maria: Proposed schema v1: `hint_profile` object with keys {workload, latency_class, model_family, experiment_tag}. Implementation detail: client submits hint_profile, runtime computes `hint_signature = sha1(sorted_kv_pairs)` and uses that as a soft routing signal. Hints expire after 1h. Telemetry will record aggregated hint_signature counts (no raw hint values).

antoine: Implementation notes: runtime index = base_pin + hint_signature weight. We use the hint signature only when it increases score beyond threshold; otherwise fallback to base_pin. Also enforce tenant scoping so hints from one tenant never affect another.

kevin: Ops question: how will this interact with Dedicated customers that require strict pin determinism? Answer: default OFF for Dedicated; must be an opt-in tenant flag. Also add an allowlist for keys in tenant config.

sam: Let's add a safety playbook: if hint-driven routing increases variance in tail latency or CPU by >10% in a rolling 1h window, automatically disable hints for that tenant and open a ticket. Also run an A/B test (10% traffic) to validate signal vs cost.

maria: Sounds good. Can someone draft a short RFC blurb listing allowed keys, example hint encodings, TTLs, and telemetry plan? @antoine @kevin volunteer?

antoine: I'll draft. I'll include a small protobuf sketch and TTL/defaults. Will also add compatibility note: clients should gracefully omit hints.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: RFC draft branch created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pin-hints-v1 — tagging reviewers @maria @antoine @kevin.

maria: Thanks — will review the draft once it's up.
